thread:
morgan (oncall): Pager: p95 routing oscillation detected for eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1 fallbacks. High churn in routing decisions over last 7m, customers reporting increased latency and a few timeouts. Paging eng-sre and runtime.
incident-bot: Incident created #INC-2026-1832004567 — Severity: S2. Alert rule: routing.p95.redispatch > 1.5x baseline. Notifying oncall.
morgan (oncall): I'm on it. Initial checks: control plane logs show repeated policy re-evaluations, reason 'latency_slo_breach' then immediate reroute to alternate region, which then reports similar p95 spike and triggers reroute back.
lexi (eng-runtime): Thanks — can you paste the recent routing decisions? I want prefix + policy id.
morgan (oncall): Pasting tail of control-plane decisions:
```
[1832004501] route_decision: model=redwood-7b-q4, region=eu-west-1, policy=latency_slo_v2, reason=p95>1200ms
[1832004522] route_decision: model=redwood-7b-q4, region=eu-central-1, policy=latency_slo_v2, reason=p95>1200ms
[1832004537] route_decision: model=redwood-7b-q4, region=eu-west-1, policy=latency_slo_v2, reason=p95>1200ms
```
morgan (oncall): Looks like same model variant being used in both regions, so fallback is not actually reducing latency — it's bouncing.
devon (eng-sre): Confirming. Metrics: both regions saw p95 jump from ~600ms -> 1.3s at same windows. CPU/GPU utilization on hosts shows short spikes but not saturated. No host-level OOMs.
tilly (prod-ops): Customer-impact: CS reporting a handful of customers with degraded chat experiences (slow responses, retries). Samir, do you have details on affected tenants?
samir (customer-success): I have three active customers flagged: AcmeCorp (eu), NodalHealth (eu), SparkEDU (global). They're seeing 5-15% request errors and increased tail latency. I'm drafting a notice but will wait for mitigation.
lexi (eng-runtime): Hypothesis: SLO-based policy triggers reroute when local p95 breaches threshold, but routing policy doesn't check variant compatibility or cache-warmth. Moving between regions with cold KV caches + identical variant means no improvement -> oscillation.
morgan (oncall): Agreed. Immediate mitigation idea: temporarily disable automatic SLO-driven region reroutes for the affected policy and set sticky routing to prefer current region for 60s.
devon (eng-sre): I can flip a policy flag. Plan: set policy.latency_slo_v2.auto_reroute=false for namespace=prod and create a sticky session TTL=60s. That should stop churn while we investigate root cause.
lexi (eng-runtime): +1. Also add a short-circuit: when fallback target uses same model variant (arch+quant), suppress reroute for 30s — avoids pointless remaps.
morgan (oncall): Doing the change now.
deploy-bot: User devon initiated a runtime config change: PATCH /policies/latency_slo_v2 {"auto_reroute":false} — change-id=chg-3821 — rolling to control-plane nodes.
devon (eng-sre): Change applied to control-plane nodes in eu region. Now applying sticky TTL.
deploy-bot: Applied sticky routing: {"policy":"latency_slo_v2","sticky_ttl_s":60} — change-id=chg-3822
morgan (oncall): Observing metrics: reroute count drops sharply. p95 in eu-west-1 slowly recovers from 1.3s -> 800ms over 4m. Error rates decreasing.
lexi (eng-runtime): While that mitigates, need root cause: logs show KV cache miss rates spiked when traffic moved between CSP pools. Maybe cache warm-up is longer than expected due to quantized model variant requiring larger KV footprints.
devon (eng-sre): I'll spin a short internal canary with warmed KV + same traffic pattern to see behavior. Also collecting GC stats and NVidia MIG metrics.
tilly (prod-ops): Samir — if recovery continues we should hold off on external comms until we have a stable mitigation. If not, we'll send interim status.
samir (customer-success): Acknowledged. I'll prepare a short holding message saying we're investigating and mitigating; will only send if we need to escalate.
lexi (eng-runtime): Also creating an emergency eval: compare redwood-7b-q4 on eu-west-1 vs eu-central-1 under identical load while tracking KV hit rate, cache size, and per-token latency. Will post results in this thread.
morgan (oncall): Oncall handoff note for next shift: if p95 redispatch rate > 5/min revert policy.flag auto_reroute=false to true? No, keep it manual until root cause fixed. Leaving note.
devon (eng-sre): Collected trace sample for a bounced request: shows cold KV lookups and repeated model reload attempts due to a transient model loader backoff. That aligns with runtime needing longer to fully serve cache-heavy traffic.
lexi (eng-runtime): OK — action items: 1) keep auto_reroute disabled for latency_slo_v2 for 2 hours 2) deploy sticky TTL=60s across all regions 3) add variant-compatibility check to routing policy logic 4) increase KV prewarm timeout for the next rollout of q4 quantized variants.
morgan (oncall): I'm documenting actions in the incident ticket. Also tagging this as 'routing:policy' and 'root_cause:cache_warmup'.
samir (customer-success): Customers notified? Hold for now. If we reach 30m with recovery >90% I'll send update saying mitigation in progress and that we're monitoring.
devon (eng-sre): Monitoring looks stable. Reroute count flattened, p95 back down to ~650-750ms in both eu regions. Error spikes resolved.
lexi (eng-runtime): I'll open a follow-up RFC to change policy semantics: require fallback to a different model family or quantization profile to qualify as a reroute target, otherwise require KV-warmup metric or a weighted cooldown.
morgan (oncall): Handoff summary for next oncall (pasteable):
- Incident: routing oscillation triggered by latency_slo_v2 (ID 1832004567)
- Impact: elevated p95 and transient errors for EU customers (AcmeCorp, NodalHealth, SparkEDU)
- Mitigation applied: auto_reroute=false, sticky_ttl=60s (chg-3821/chg-3822)
- Current state: stable, p95 recovered to ~700ms, reroutes stopped
- Next steps: runtime ticket for variant-compatibility check, KV prewarm adjustments, RFC for policy semantics
- If reroutes resume: runbook step A1 -> roll forward sticky TTL 120s, escalate to SRE lead

tilly (prod-ops): Thanks team. Marking incident as 'mitigated' pending postmortem. I'll schedule a 30min follow-up postmortem in 48h.
incident-bot: Incident #INC-2026-1832004567 status updated to MITIGATED by morgan. Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2026-04-01T15:00:00Z.
morgan (oncall): Thx all. I'll draft the impact blurb and include timeline + diffs of policy config changes.
samir (customer-success): I'll coordinate customer comms after postmortem draft. Stand down unless it flares back.
lexi (eng-runtime): Adding note: this is a near-miss for policy design — avoid relying solely on latency SLO without model-variant/cold-cache signals. Will include metrics in RFC.
morgan (oncall): Closing thread for now. If anyone sees any regressions ping me directly. :thermometer_face:
